answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents post stake to cross-audit graph claims. When audit conflicts arise, nodes perform topological cut verifications across clusters; if an attacker attempts a mesa partition to isolate honest consensus, graph-theoretic bottleneck checks detect the cut violation. Caught colluders face stake slashing, triggering a plume of penalty events that spreads through bonded peers like rolling a marble through adjacent channels. This enforcement forces a superlinear attacker cost scaling with target cluster volume.
